---
title: "annotation-gate.yml"
---

Fail a run that carries an annotation nobody allowed.

A check that emits a `::warning::` or `::notice::` on a green job tells the
reader something is wrong without stopping the merge, and agents and authors
skip it.
This gate reads the annotations of every other job in the run through the
check-runs API and fails when any `notice`, `warning` or `failure` annotation
does not match an allow pattern.

## Use

Add one job that lists every other job in `needs` and runs `if: always()`.
See `examples/annotation-gate.yml`.
Grant the job `actions: read`, `checks: read` and `contents: read`.

## Inputs

- `levels`: levels to enforce, default `notice,warning,failure`.
- `allow-patterns`: newline-separated case-insensitive regexes for tracked
  exceptions.
- `job-name`: optional extra name prefix of a job to skip.
  The gate's own job is always skipped, whatever the caller named it.

The composite action `Morrison-Lab/gha/annotation-gate@v3` also takes
`default-allow`, which replaces the allowed-for-everyone list below, and `token`.
The reusable workflow keeps the defaults.
It takes three more inputs for the `workflow_run` mode described at the end:
`run-id` (the run to gate instead of the current one), `run-attempt`, and
`head-sha` (post the result as a check run on this commit).

## Allowed for everyone

- GitHub's runner-image migration notice ("The ubuntu-latest label will
  migrate to ...").
- A job's own "Process completed with exit code N" failure annotation.
  A failed job already fails the run, and the gate runs under `if: always()`,
  so this one would only repeat it.
- The forced-Node deprecation warning, until the action pins are bumped.
  It reads "Node.js N is deprecated" and then "The following actions target Node".
- The two annotations the review workflow emits when a newer push supersedes
  a review: the concurrency group's "Canceling since a higher priority waiting
  request for ..." and the stale-review skip "PR head moved ...; not posting a
  stale review".
  Both describe a run that was meant to stop, and the newer push gets its own review.
- The notice the review workflow emits on a PR that edits workflow files:
  "PR edits workflow files; restored .github/workflows/ from the default
  branch ...".
  It reports the safe behavior of gha#598, so it is not a defect in the PR.

## Scope

Annotations from the gate's own job, and from a job that has not finished,
are not seen.
A reusable-workflow job is covered, because the jobs endpoint lists each by
its full name.

## One gate for a repository with many workflow files

The job above sees only the jobs of its own run.
A repository whose checks live in separate workflow files calls
`annotation-gate-run.yml` from one `workflow_run` workflow instead.
It gates each run that finishes and posts the result as a check run named
`annotation-gate` on that run's commit, so it shows on the pull request.

```yaml
name: Annotation gate
on: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers] -- the gate checks out nothing and runs no code from the triggering run
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["*"]
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  gate:
    # The gate's own run must not trigger another gate.
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.name != 'Annotation gate' }}
    permissions:
      actions: read
      checks: write
      contents: read
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/annotation-gate-run.yml@v3
    with:
      run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
      run-attempt: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt }}
      head-sha: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
```

It takes the same `levels` and `allow-patterns` inputs.
Grant `checks: write`; the job posts one check run per gated run.

Each gated run posts its own check run named `annotation-gate`.
When several workflows finish on one commit, the commit carries several checks
of that name, and a failing one blocks a required check.
`annotation-gate-run.yml` holds `checks: write`, so it is not in the
read-only list on the permissions page.
It calls the action at `@v3`, so it gates the right run only once `v3` has
slid past the commit that added these inputs; before that the unknown inputs
are ignored and the gate checks its own run.
See `examples/annotation-gate-run.yml` for the stub to copy.
